{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Makes ONE long picture from a folder of photos, side by side, like a photo booth strip or a before and after row. No AI is used: it shows how a loop can build one result from many pictures.

 Pick your folder

  1. On Load Images from Folder Pixaroma, click Browse and pick your folder, or paste the folder's path into the box.
  2. Click Pick images, then Select all, or click only the pictures you want. The button shows how many are picked.
  3. Press Run once. Leave the Run count at 1: the node sends every picture through by itself, one after the other.

This workflow opens with no folder picked: choose your own folder, or try it first on the demo folder Portraits inside the Media Inputs folder that comes with these workflows.

 A folder inside ComfyUI's own input or output folder works straight away. A folder anywhere else works too, but pick it once with Browse: that is how ComfyUI knows you allowed it.

 Pictures go through in name order. Name them 01_, 02_ and so on if the order matters.

 Change the look

  • The size of each photo: Resize Crop Pixaroma.
  • The gap and its color: spacing_width and spacing_color on Stitch Images.
  • A tall strip instead of a wide one: set the direction on Stitch Images to up.

 How a loop works

  • Everything between Loop Start and Loop End runs again and again: total on Loop Start says how many rounds.
  • Loop Start's index says which round it is, counting from 0 (0, 1, 2, 3). A Math Expression turns it into what you need: a + 1 for 1, 2, 3, 4, or a + b to add it to a seed.
  • The value slots carry things from one round to the next. What you plug into Loop End's value1 comes out of Loop Start's value1 in the NEXT round. After the last round it comes out of Loop End.
  • Wire Loop Start's loop output into Loop End's loop input: that is how the two know they belong together.

 This loop needs no count from you: Get Image Size counts the photos and sets the rounds. Wiring a number into total like this works on any loop.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Folder not approved Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Images from Folder Pixaroma (1. your folder) - Point it at a folder and pick the pictures. Press Run once and it sends every picture through the workflow, one after the other. Its filename output carries each picture's name to the save node, and index says which picture it is (1, 2, 3 ...).
  • Resize Crop Pixaroma (2. size of each photo) - Makes every photo the same square size, here 512 x 512. They must all be the same size to go into one batch.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves and do the small jobs: count, pick, join or pass things along.

  • Rebatch Images (all photos into one batch) - Collects the photos, which the folder node sends one by one, back into ONE batch, so the loop can pick them by number.
  • Get Image Size (batch_size = how many photos) - Its batch_size output is the number of photos in the batch. It is wired into Loop Start's total, so the loop runs exactly once per photo, however many you pick.
  • Loop Start Pixaroma (one round per photo) - Opens the loop. total comes from Get Image Size (one round per photo). value1 carries the strip built so far: empty in round 1.
  • Loop End Pixaroma (sends the strip to the next round) - Closes the loop and hands the longer strip to the next round. After the last round, value1 is the finished strip.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • Image From Batch (this round's photo) - Takes ONE photo out of the batch: the one at this round's index (0 = the first photo).
  • Stitch Images (adds it to the right of the strip) - Joins this round's photo and the strip so far into one picture, with a 16 px white gap. Direction left puts the old strip on the left, so the photos stay in order. In round 1 there is no strip yet, so the photo goes through alone.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (the finished strip) - Saves the strip as JPG into ComfyUI/output/Photo Strip.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.
